title: Poon Lim — 133 days alone on a raft
sources: Wikipedia: Poon Lim (8 March 1918 – 4 January 1991) — Chinese seafarer, Second Mess Steward on the British cargo ship SS Benlomond; on 23 November 1942 the German submarine U-172 hit her with two torpedoes about 400 km off Brazil and she sank in about two minutes; Poon was washed overboard; the U-boat crew saw him, laughed and waved him away; after about two hours he boarded an 8-ft (2.4 m) wooden life raft stocked with water, hardtack, chocolate, pemmican, milk and flares; the food ran out after about 55 days; he made a fish hook from the spring of a flashlight, caught fish and seabirds and dried the meat; with no rain, he caught a shark, beat it to death with a water container and drank blood from its liver; ships passed without stopping; a US Navy patrol plane saw him and dropped a marker, but a storm hid him; he counted days with knots, then counted full moons; on 5 April 1943 three Brazilian fishermen found him off Pará, after 133 days and about 1,210 km of drift; he was the sole survivor of Benlomond; he had lost 9 kg and walked again within days; King George VI awarded him the British Empire Medal and the Royal Navy put his story into its survival manuals; told no one had survived longer on a raft, he said: 'I hope no one will ever have to break that record.'

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / US Navy / US National Archives / Imperial War Museum): Poon Lim with US Navy officers, 1943; a reconstruction of his raft made for US Navy survival training; U-172 on the surface, 1943; a torpedoed Allied tanker; Allied survivors on life rafts

Archive film (public domain / CC0): Universal Newsreel — the tanker R. P. Resor torpedoed by a U-boat, 1942 (timecode cropped); 'Battle in Atlantic between British Navy and Bismarck' (1941); 'Life and Death of USS Hornet' (US Navy, 1943) — illustrative
Music: Eternal Father, Strong to Save (the Navy Hymn) — United States Navy Band, public domain

post.facebook:
For 133 days, he drifted alone across the Atlantic, on a raft smaller than a car.

Poon Lim was a young steward from China on the British cargo ship Benlomond. In November 1942 a German submarine hit her with two torpedoes and she sank in two minutes. Poon was thrown into the sea; the U-boat crew saw him, laughed and waved him away. After two hours in the water he found an empty life raft, with water and biscuits for weeks — not months.

When the food ran out, he made a fish hook from the spring of a flashlight. He caught fish and seabirds and dried their meat in the sun. When the rain stopped, he caught a shark, beat it to death and drank the blood from its liver. Ships passed him by; a Navy plane spotted him, then a storm hid him again. He stopped counting days and started counting full moons.

In April 1943, three Brazilian fishermen found him close to the shore — the only survivor of his ship. The King gave him a medal and the Royal Navy put his tricks into its survival manuals. Told no one had survived longer on a raft, he said: "I hope no one will ever have to break that record."

youtube.description:
For 133 days, he drifted alone across the Atlantic, on a raft smaller than a car.

Poon Lim, a Chinese steward on the British ship Benlomond, survived the sinking by U-172 in November 1942 — the U-boat crew saw him and laughed. He fished with a hook made from a flashlight spring, caught seabirds and a shark, and drifted about 1,200 km until Brazilian fishermen found him in April 1943, the only survivor of his ship. He received the British Empire Medal and his methods went into Royal Navy survival manuals.
